question: In the forward osmosis experiments, what COD and osmotic pressure did the municipal wastewater feed have?
rendered:
<document title="A Comparative Study of Forward Osmosis Systems: An Integrated Experimental, Modeling, and Techno-Economic Analysis">

=== page 2 ===
- Deionized water (DI), characterized by a conductivity below 2 μS cm^− 1, and real municipal wastewater (WW), with a chemical oxygen demand (COD) of 460 mg L^− 1 and an osmotic pressure of 2.5 bar were employed as feed solutions.
- The wastewater was sourced from the secondary clarifier effluent of a local municipal treatment plant, and was pre-filtered through a 0.45 μm membrane filter before use.
- Draw solutions were prepared to provide an initial nominal osmotic pressure of 30 bar at 25 °C, using analytical-grade salts: NaCl (35.0 g L^−1), MgSO4·7H2O (71.8 g L^−1), and sodium acetate (79.4 g L^−1).

The answer is: The municipal wastewater feed had a COD of 460 mg L^− 1 and an osmotic pressure of 2.5 bar.
